verdict: 16 Oct 2026 refresh: RBI MPC on 7 Oct 2026 raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% with stance shifting to 'calibrated tightening' — first repo hike since Feb 2023 — and EBLR-linked home-loan rates will reset upward within one cycle (SBI floor ~7.50%, HDFC ~8.00% after pass-through). Anarock Q3 2026 city release shows Bengaluru supply (17,720 units) outpacing sales (16,670) and top-7 unsold inventory at ~6.31 lakh units (+12% YoY). Knight Frank H1 2026 Bengaluru EMI/income still 35% but mechanically re-prices toward ~36–37% once the hike flows through. Karnataka April 2026 guidance-value revision still ungazetted; IGR monthly aggregates for Jul/Aug/Sep still unpublished. Composite tilt: UP — tightening cycle resumed while supply overhang widens.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.value: Top-7 unsold ~6.31 lakh units (+12% YoY) Q3 2026; Bengaluru launches 17,720 > sales 16,670
indicators.note: Anarock Q3 2026: pan-India unsold across top-7 cities ~6,30,590 units (+12% YoY from ~5,61,760). Q3 launches 1,14,320 exceeded sales 1,00,220 by ~14,100 — Bengaluru city read-out: new supply 17,720 units vs sales 16,670. Implied clearance ~19 months at current absorption pace. Overhang still concentrated in East Bengaluru (Whitefield, Sarjapur). Status kept amber — worsening but not yet red; QTS still manageable in North/East.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.value: Top-7 Q3 2026: ~24% in ₹1.5–2.5Cr, 34% in ₹80L–1.5Cr, only ~14% below ₹40L; Bengaluru ₹2–5Cr unsold +153% YoY (H1 2026)
indicators.note: Anarock Q3 2026 ticket-size table shows ≥₹1.5Cr accounting for roughly a quarter of launches top-7; sub-₹50 lakh Bengaluru stock remains in long-tail with Knight Frank QTS ~21.4. H1 2026 trend of ₹2–5Cr unsold +153% YoY in Bengaluru persists. Developers continue to pivot to premium as mid-segment demand thins. Status unchanged — red.

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.value: 35% (Knight Frank H1 2026); RBI repo hiked 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 — pass-through pending
indicators.note: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026: Bengaluru EMI/income at 35%. RBI MPC on 7 Oct 2026 raised repo 25 bps (5.25%→5.50%) and shifted stance to 'calibrated tightening' — first hike since Feb 2023. EBLR-linked home loans reset within one cycle; illustrative ₹50L/20Y EMI up ~₹795/mo, ~₹1.91L extra interest over tenure. Ratio mechanically re-prices toward ~36–37% once the hike lands in borrower EMIs. Typical home-loan rates now ~7.50–8.25% (SBI floor ~7.50%, HDFC ~8.00%). Status kept amber — still inside Knight Frank's 50% threshold but trending wrong way. H2 2026 KF release due Dec 2026.

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report June 2026: housing-loan GNPA at 0.5%; system GNPA at multi-decade low of 1.8% (Mar 2026), projected to rise only to 1.9% by Mar 2028 under baseline. Secured retail GNPA 0.7%; unsecured retail 1.7% flagged for watch as non-housing retail now 58.4% of household borrowing. CRAR 17.7%, CET1 15.3%. Next FSR expected Dec 2026 — no October release. Unchanged from 28 Sep 2026.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.value: Indiranagar asking 50–80% over guidance; Devanahalli/Hoskote 15–25%; April 2026 revision still not gazetted (as of 16 Oct 2026)
indicators.note: Indiranagar guidance ~₹12k/sqft vs asking ₹18–22k/sqft (50–83% premium). Newer corridors (Devanahalli, Hoskote) narrower at 15–25% and partially compressed after the Feb 2026 BBMP guidance hike (6–15%). The statewide 10–15% (up to 30% in select micro-markets) revision proposed 14 April 2026 remains not gazette-notified as of 16 Oct 2026 — sub-registrars still split on which value to apply. Bengaluru asking prices rose 8–9% YoY while registered values held at stale 2023 benchmarks. Persistent wide gap in prime pockets remains a clear froth signal; gazette landing would be a further red-tilt trigger.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Karnataka FY25–26 stamps revenue ~₹20,837 cr (record); Jul/Aug/Sep 2026 monthly still not published; stamp duty hike (6.6%→7.6%) under discussion
indicators.note: Karnataka Stamps & Registration posted a record ~₹20,837 cr in FY25–26 (largely Bengaluru). Headline revenue inflated by Aug 2025 fee doubling (1%→2%) and Feb 2026 guidance hike — volume growth softer than revenue growth. Q1 FY26 showed ~35% shortfall vs ₹7,000 cr target with Bengaluru registrations down 21% in June; FY26 target revised to ₹28,000 cr. A further stamp-duty hike (6.6%→7.6%) still under discussion but unimplemented, suggesting continued pressure on volumes. IGR Karnataka has not published Jul/Aug/Sep 2026 monthly aggregates as of 16 Oct 2026. Kaveri 3.0 (AI-driven) rollout still flagged for FY26–27.
